value.body: A two-year master's in history. You study periods (ancient, medieval, modern), regions and themes such as economic, social or art history, and learn to work with primary sources and historiography. Many universities offer specialisations such as archaeology, museology or archival studies as electives.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 semesters; also offered through distance and open universities

items.label: PG students in history
items.note: One of the larger PG disciplines in the humanities
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 13, based on actual responses (Ministry of Education)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree (usually in history or any arts subject, depending on the university). Central and many state universities admit through CUET-PG; others hold their own entrance test or admit on graduation marks.

value.title: At a glance
items: School teaching (PGT) needs a B.Ed along with the master's; college teaching needs UGC-NET or a PhD.
Heritage work — archives, museums, archaeology — usually needs a further specialised diploma or degree, and posts are limited.
History is a common optional subject in civil services exams.
Writing, research and editorial roles are also open to history postgraduates.
